clues.kinetics: Orally administered drug is well absorbed, and food slows absorption without reducing its extent. It is 40% bound to plasma proteins, and hepatic metabolism accounts for approximately 85% of elimination.
clues.substance: Molecular weight 293.4. It has moderate aqueous solubility, independent of pH in the physiological range.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA, supplied in bottles of 30 and taken once daily.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients; hot flashes and arthralgia are among the common reactions, at 10% or more.
clues.indication: Adjuvant treatment of early hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, first-line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic disease, and advanced disease after tamoxifen, all in postmenopausal women.
clues.mechanism: A selective non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor that blocks conversion of androgens to estrone and estradiol, lowering serum estradiol without affecting adrenal corticosteroids or aldosterone.

tell: Hepatic metabolism accounts for about 85% of elimination, and its main circulating metabolite, triazole, is inactive.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: maximum plasma concentrations typically occur within 2 hours of dosing under fasted conditions
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: The mean elimination half-life of anastrozole is 50 hours
